speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This need is now more pressing as global tax trends rapidly shift with the implementation of the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 guidelines.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's longstanding ability to attract global businesses is grounded in a combination of factors: our stable political climate, robust infrastructure, skilled workforce and competitive fiscal policies.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, we now face a critical moment where Singapore must balance these advantages with evolving international tax obligations to maintain our position as a premier hub for business and investment.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This highlights the importance of continuing to attract foreign investments and global talent that complement our local workforce and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is a necessary step to align with international standards while continuing to combat aggressive tax planning practices.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, we must recognise that the impact on our business community will be significant and multi-faceted.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While ensuring MNEs contribute fairly to our economy, we must be mindful of the challenges these new rules will bring.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Compliance costs and administrative burdens will likely rise for companies operating across multiple jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As our MNEs face higher compliance and administrative burdens, many jurisdictions, such as Switzerland, Ireland and Thailand, are implementing significant tax reforms in response to the global minimum tax.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In light of these global shifts, I would like to ask the Minister how Singapore plans to mitigate any competitiveness concerns.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Our competitors' actions may erode Singapore's traditional strengths.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Will the Government consider enhancing non-tax incentives in areas, such as infrastructure, talent development and support for research and development (R&D) and innovation to maintain our attractiveness for foreign investments?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While the BEPS Pillar Two taxation framework is largely standardised across implementing jurisdictions, the implementation and administrative rules are not as strictly defined by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister clarify whether Singapore has room for flexibility in these administrative processes?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, could Singapore adopt simplified compliance procedures or introduce a more lenient enforcement framework during the initial stages of the Bill's implementation to help businesses ease into the new regime?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore has historically demonstrated an ability to adapt flexibly within global frameworks and we should continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Our transparent and predictable tax regime is a unique advantage that enhances our appeal as a jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For example, companies can be assured of the non-taxation of capital gains on certain equity disposals, provided they meet specific criteria under the law.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has also provided useful guidance via its e-Tax Guide.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Such clear guidelines, not easily found in other jurisdictions, offer businesses confidence and certainty in their operations.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: My recommendation is that we should build on these strengths by expanding and leveraging clear guidelines that offer businesses confidence and certainty, further solidifying Singapore as a business-friendly environment.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Moving on to the operational and compliance challenges posed by the MMT Bill, it is essential to recognise that MNE groups within the scope of Pillar Two will be required to register with the Comptroller within six months after the relevant financial year ends.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: These groups will also need to designate local entities for filing GloBE information returns and the domestic top-up tax (DTT) returns.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, there are other surcharges and penalties which can apply as outlined in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For example, furnishing an incorrect tax return without reasonable excuse can result in penalties of up to two times the tax undercharged.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While these penalties are meant to ensure compliance, their significant financial impact should not be underestimated.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister clarify whether additional guidelines will be provided to streamline the registration process and explain when penalty might be waived?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Given that this is a significant new requirement, many companies may face difficulties in meeting the deadline, particularly if they are cross-border entities with complex organisational structures.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Minister consider introducing a grace period during the early stages of implementation, whereby penalties and sanctions would not apply if an MNE demonstrates that it made reasonable efforts to comply?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This would alleviate concerns within the business community and offer some flexibility as companies adapt to the new requirements.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill also mandates that MNE group entities keep sufficient records to allow the Comptroller to verify the top-up tax payable.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, different entities and periods may be subject to varying record-keeping requirements, potentially increasing the administrative burden on companies.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister assure us that these variations in record-keeping periods will be minimised and aligned, as much as possible, with the existing five-year standard for income tax matters?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This would help reduce administrative burden on businesses.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, investing in IRAS' capacity to administer and enforce these complex new rules effectively will be crucial to ensuring a smooth and efficient implementation process.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: SMEs, the backbone of our economy, often face challenges in securing capital for innovation, technology upgrades and productivity improvements.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The refundability of the RIC provides much-needed liquidity, allowing them to reinvest in their businesses and address a core issue – cash flow management.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As we refine the RIC, it is crucial that it remains flexible in its design.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: High-value activities like R&D, digital transformation and sustainability initiatives often take time to yield results.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: A rigid, outcome-based approach could discourage investment in long-term projects with uncertain short-term returns.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The RIC must allow businesses to pursue innovative activities without the fear of disqualification due to delayed results.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This is especially critical for SMEs, which face significant upfront costs and may not see immediate success.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This flexibility ensures that businesses can invest confidently in long-term growth without being constrained by rigid criteria.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The RIC should also support Singapore's transition to a sustainable economy.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Given our limited space, consideration could be given to overseas or cross border green projects as long as the ideation, key knowledge, project management and talent associated with the project remain in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Expanding the RIC to incentivise green investments will help align our fiscal policies with Singapore's sustainability goals, positioning us as a global leader in green innovation.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By striking the right balance between flexibility and a focus on long-term outcomes and by expanding initiatives like the RIC to incentivise green investments, we can ensure that Singapore remains a leader in both economic, innovation and environmental stewardship.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is important to continuously assess the impact of these changes and be agile in adapting our approach to ensure Singapore remains an attractive and competitive global business hub.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Both these Bills work hand in hand to ensure Singapore remains competitive in the global marketplace, yet they do so in complementary but contrasting ways – one offering relief, while the other enforces a stricter regime.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Both promote fairness and transparency in our tax regime.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I believe these amendments will encourage foreign investment and help sustain our economic growth by enhancing Singapore's global competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill also provides enhanced tax deductions for R&D, encouraging companies to invest in high-tech and green technologies.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This will bolster Singapore's position as a leader in innovation and future industries, driving sustainable economic growth.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Simplified tax administration will also make it easier for businesses to comply with tax regulations.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, the RIC benefits businesses and encourages investment and capital expenditures, R&D and talent development.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The RIC also helps businesses offset the corporate tax liabilities, making it more attractive to establish many factoring facilities and regional headquarters in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, the Bill encourages focus on decarbonisation efforts, aligning with our broader sustainability goals.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By adopting this Bill, Singapore aligns itself with global tax transparency efforts, ensuring that large MNEs contribute their fair share to our economy.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The revenue generated through this minimum tax will safeguard the Government's financial base, allowing us to invest in infrastructure, social programmes and growth initiatives.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments will ensure that Singapore can create a more predictable and consistent tax landscape, a critical factor for MNEs that evaluate where to base their operations.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, the Bill promotes fairness by addressing the competitive disadvantages faced by local businesses, especially SMEs, when competing against MNEs.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By enforcing a minimum tax, we are fostering fair competition and supporting the long-term sustainability of both our local businesses and our tax system.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: One, how will businesses currently benefiting from existing tax incentives be affected by these amendments?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Will their exemptions continue under the new framework, or will they be required to re-apply?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Two, how will the minimum tax rate apply to industries with unique tax treatments, such as financial services, energy or digital businesses?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Will specific sectors receive special considerations or exemptions?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Three, how do the new regulations align with Singapore's existing international tax treaties and agreements, specifically regarding parenting double taxation and resolving disputes?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be any adjustments required to ensure compatibility with the global minimum tax framework?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Four, what penalties will be imposed on businesses that fail to meet the compliance requirements, particularly in sectors like financial services and for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Are there limits or caps on the amount of tax credited can be refunded through the RIC?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By balancing the need for fairness, transparency and innovation, these Bills will help ensure our long-term economic growth while addressing the challenges posed by global tax trends.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Pillar One reallocates taxing rights to market jurisdictions, posing a challenge for Singapore given our small domestic market.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Pillar Two establishes a 15% minimum effective tax rate for MNEs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In my speech, I will address three key points: firstly, the unintended consequences of implementing DTT and income inclusion rule under BEPS 2.0 Pillar Two; secondly, clarifications on the RIC; and thirdly, the timing of this implementation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Investments inject capital, create jobs and nurture local talent.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They foster competitiveness, innovation and technology transfers through global partnerships.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To stay relevant, we must secure the right investments that refresh industries, attract expertise and adopt emerging technologies and shape our future economy.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Investments across diverse sectors, such as the digital services and green technologies, strengthens resilience against economic shocks.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The investments reinforce our role as a global hub and aligned with environmental plans, preparing Singapore for future challenges.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we support BEPS 2.0's goal of ensuring MNEs pay their fair share, implementing DTT and income inclusion rule could impact Singapore's attractiveness as an investment destination.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Singapore's strategic location, skilled workforce and low corporate taxes are all critical to attracting investments.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, the 15% minimum effective tax rate could reduce the effectiveness of our tax incentives, making other jurisdictions more attractive.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the minimum effective tax rate may increase short-term tax revenue, MNEs could adjust strategies by relocating operations or headquarters, limiting sustainable gains.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Competing countries may also improve other factors, such as access to land and skilled labour, where Singapore faces inherent constraints.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the next investment cycle, if businesses scale back their investments into Singapore, or diversify their investments away from Singapore or explore other options, this could negatively affect employment and economic growth in sectors such as finance, technology and manufacturing.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Following suit, sectors like logistics, pharmaceuticals and real estate may also feel the pressure.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, we must strike a balance: closing international tax gaps while ensuring that BEPS 2.0 does not inadvertently disadvantage Singapore or limit future opportunities.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As we comply with BEPS 2.0, the RIC strengthens our ability to attract investments.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has also clarified that the RIC is treated as a grant under section 93B.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: RIC incentivises activities such as new manufacturing plants and low-carbon energy projects, expansion in digital services, supply chain management, headquarters operations, R&D and decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: More importantly, it also covers critical costs, including capital investments and investments in our workforce.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have a few questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can qualifying activities include finance, insurance, aviation and investment in artificial intelligence (AI), given their importance to Singapore's economy?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What criteria will the Economic Development Board (EBD) and EnterpriseSG use to determine the total RIC quantum a company is eligible for?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Why is the RIC payout spread over four years?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could an earlier payout support higher investment hurdles?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The evolving global tax landscape requires us to monitor developments closely and adapt our strategies to attract investments vital to our economy's future.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some Members shared the view that the implementation of BEPS 2.0 will be a windfall or generate clear net benefit for Singapore as it will have a muted effect on investments, a view by Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And in some instances, Members go even as far as planning our operating expenditure from this uncertain perceived benefit.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am glad that Members Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Mr Louis Chua and Ms Hazel Poa, in their speeches yesterday have acknowledged the various factors that attract investments into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These include our skilled and educated workforce, robust infrastructure and technological advancements, political stability and a strong legal framework, including citing that Singapore is number one in IMD World Competitiveness Ranking.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Their recognition highlights the effectiveness of the sound, long-term policies implemented by our People's Action Party (PAP) Government and our continued investments in our skilled workforce, advanced infrastructure and the importance of our tripartism.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It cites that the third lever of alternative sources of revenue to the GST hike is the increase in corporate taxation due to BEPS 2.0 and went on to mention "each of these levers  , when pulled, could yield more revenues, equal or more than the GST hike", implying that the uncertain perceived net outcome of BEPS 2.0 can, on its own, fund the certainty of our increased healthcare cost.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the second example, Mr Louis Chua, in his Budget speech on 26 February, on the topic of RIC and BEPS 2.0, shared that "it would be a sad day if countries go against the spirit of the reforms in the first place" and hopes that "additional tax revenue from BEPS 2.0 will not simply be in substance returned to the MNEs through other forms", views which he reiterated against yesterday.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: That said, in my professional capacity as someone who is from the industry whose responsibilities is to look at where and how MNEs invest in factories and technology developments globally, I do caution against propagating these two simplistic views.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While various factors contribute to a country's attractiveness, tax remains a factor to consider in building a compelling business case when trying to cut across the investment hurdle, especially when we consider the differential cost of labour, the cost of land, the cost of construction and the increasing grants that are offered in other jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And as Members rightfully pointed out, we need to increase spending to strengthen key attraction factors, such as investing more in our workforce and enhancing productivity, objectives that clearly align closely with the intent of the RIC.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, the net effect of BEPS 2.0 remains uncertain at this point, especially when Pillar One has not been considered.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given the uncertainty surrounding BEPS 2.0, we must avoid equating non-inevitable costs, such as rising healthcare expenses, with the uncertain outcomes of BEPS 2.0 implementation, which is still in its early stages.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is unwise to base essential fiscal policies like healthcare spending on unpredictable future revenues.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we do our part and comply with the global BEPS 2.0 rollout, we must be cautious not to restrict our investment attraction toolkit.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This grant focuses on developing new productive capacity, advancing R&D, fostering innovation and supporting decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Most importantly, the grant also covers key costs, such as capital expenditure and investment in our workforce, an objective that many Members in this debate have also reiterated.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is a grant to attract high-value, high-quality investments into Singapore, which are our lifeblood for our survival.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In both examples, it is evident that we cannot gamble the future healthcare needs of Singapore with uncertain revenue streams, such as the perceived gains from BEPS 2.0, nor double dip it.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Nor should we gamble the future opportunities for our next generation by restricting schemes, such as RIC, which will limit our ability to attract good, high-value investments to provide good jobs for our people, especially in light of increasing competition to attract investments.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given the competition for investment, is there an opportunity for us to delay the implementation?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While some Members may opine that the effects may be muted, the criticality of it means that we must tread carefully to avoid the unintended consequences that could weaken our investment ecosystem and economic resilience.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The introduction of RIC is a vital tool in our strategy, helping us comply with global tax rules while attracting the right investments to sustain growth and innovation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is an investment attraction tool that can help us shape our future economy.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We must remain vigilant, adaptive and proactive in adjusting our investment toolkit to maintain Singapore's competitiveness in a rapidly changing global environment.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our objective must be clear: close gaps in international tax rules, ensuring multinational enterprises (MNEs) pay their fair share, and safeguard Singapore's future opportunities, all while planning prudently for the long term.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Notwithstanding the clarifications above, I stand in support of the Bill, Mdm Deputy Speaker.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Most of the Members who had spoken touched on the newly introduced RIC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am glad that Members agree that this is a timely and important move to ensure that we attract and support businesses that undertake substantive and high-value economic activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members' questions generally related to: (a) the types of activities supported; (b) the design; (c) the total amount awarded; and (d) the budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Mark Lee spoke on the need to keep the RIC flexible such that it would also support high-value activities that can only realise benefits in the long term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Indeed, we recognise that investments in innovation, R&D and sustainability will take time to bear fruit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For these, we require the RIC to be awarded based on expenditure with clear outcomes, within a reasonable timeframe commensurate with the type of activity undertaken.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is to ensure that the RIC supports projects that benefit our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Mark Lee also asked whether the RIC scope could be expanded to include activities, such as finance, insurance, aviation and overseas or cross-border green projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For a start, we have designed the RIC to support the qualifying activities announced at Budget this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, we thank Mr Lee and Mr Sharael for their suggestions and will continue to monitor industry demand and trends, and assess how the RIC can be updated to remain competitive and relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked about the payout schedule of the RIC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This means that companies can start to benefit by using the RICs to offset their corporate income tax payable once they are awarded the credits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill allows for regulations to enable RIC recipients to choose to receive the RIC in cash instead of being offset in taxes and Mr Louis Chua asked for the rationale for this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are considering such a feature as some companies have provided feedback that an option for the RIC to be paid in cash over a fixed schedule would provide greater cash flow certainty.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As explained in my opening speech, the RIC is an expenditure-based grant delivered through the tax system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The net fiscal impact to the Government is the same, whether the RIC is used to offset taxes or is refunded in cash.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Louis Chua also asked about the rationale for allowing RIC recipients to offset the taxes of related companies in the same group.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Sometimes, companies may set up separate legal entities to better reflect the structure of their business and for risk management purposes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By segregating business activities, companies can better limit their liabilities and protect the assets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, for instance, a parent Company A that invests in a new manufacturing plant in Singapore may choose to set up a subsidiary Company B to hire workers and hold the plant assets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By allowing the RIC to be offset against taxes of related companies, we provide flexibility for such business structures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For all intents and purposes, the parent company is still making the investment in Singapore, the net fiscal impact remains the same and the underlying principle of supporting qualifying local expenditure incurred also remains unchanged.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how our economic agencies would determine the total RIC quantum that a company would be eligible for and the total budget and funding for the RIC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The RIC support would be commensurate with the size and quality of businesses' economic contributions to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Companies that invest more in Singapore or commit higher quality investments will receive more support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The RIC will draw from the same funding sources that support the other schemes in our economic toolkit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include our economic agencies' annual budgets as well as the National Productivity Fund (NPF).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our economic agencies will be publishing more details of the RIC soon to provide further clarity to businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, let me address Members' comments on the MMT Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These broadly relate to: (a) the operation of the Pillar Two rules; (b) the consistency of GLoBE implementation across jurisdictions; (c) the compliance burden of the DTT and multinational enterprise top-up tax (MTT); (d) estimated revenue impact and use of revenues; and (e) economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members have sought clarifications on how the DTT and MTT will operate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Neil Parekh and Mr Louis Chua asked how the DTT and MTT would affect specific groups of businesses, such as existing tax incentive recipients and businesses in certain sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The DTT and MTT will apply to all large MNE groups with a global revenue of at least €750 million in at least two of the four preceding financial years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: DTT and MTT apply to such MNE groups in all sectors unless specific exclusions under the GLoBE rules are applicable, such as for international shipping income.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: DTT and MTT also apply, regardless of whether the large MNE group is a tax incentive recipient.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Don Wee asked how double taxation under the MTT would be prevented.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The GLoBE rules provide for the order of imposition of top-up taxes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, DTT will apply before any MTT imposed by other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This ensures that taxing rights are coordinated and prevents multiple jurisdictions from imposing top-up taxes on the same income.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Don Wee also asked about the exclusion of investment entities from the DTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The exclusion is allowed under the GLoBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Apart from Singapore, several other jurisdictions have also taken a similar approach.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For an entity to qualify as an investment entity, it must meet the requirements specified in the GLoBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The exclusion is to preserve tax neutrality such that the income of the investment entity is only taxed once at the investor level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As with all other rules, MOF and IRAS will monitor and ensure that the rules are applied as intended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Louis Chua also asked about the implementation of the subject-to-tax rule (STTR).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The STTR defines "developing countries" for its purposes as those with gross national income per capita below a specified threshold level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore does not qualify under this specific definition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a member of the Inclusive Framework, Singapore is prepared to implement STTR in our tax treaties with developing Inclusive Framework members when requested by them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can be done bilaterally or by signing the multilateral instrument.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are studying the best way to implement STTR.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about the mechanisms to ensure consistency in the implementation of GLoBE rules across jurisdictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas also asked about the impact on Singapore's DTT and MTT if China and the US do not implement the GLoBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Sharael Taha shared the same concern and asked if we should delay our implementation of DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, many jurisdictions have either implemented similar rules or intend to do so in 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The GLoBE rules have been agreed by more than 140 members of the OECD Inclusive Framework, including China and the US.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Inclusive Framework members that implement the GLoBE rules must do so in a way that is consistent with the outcomes provided for under the rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There will be a peer review process to assess jurisdictions' implementation for consistency with the rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: All Inclusive Framework members, including those that do not implement the GLoBE rules, are required to accept the application of the GLoBE rules by other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas and Mr Neil Parekh also asked about the dispute resolution process for the GLoBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is broad international agreement that a robust dispute resolution mechanism is important for MNEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, discussions on the details are still ongoing at the Inclusive Framework.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF and IRAS are participating in these discussions and will provide guidance when there is greater clarity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas and Mr Neil Parekh also asked whether the GLoBE rules would affect Singapore's network of Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Based on guidance from the Inclusive Framework, the GLoBE rules are compatible with international taxation agreements like our DTAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The vast majority of our treaty partners are members of the Inclusive Framework and have agreed to these rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members, including Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Usha Chandradas, Mr Mark Lee and Mr Don Wee, have suggested simplifying the administration of the DTT and MTT to reduce the compliance burden on affected MNE groups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF and IRAS have simplified the administrative requirements where possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, an affected MNE group will only be required to register with IRAS once, for both DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also aligned the filing timelines for DTT and MTT returns to simplify compliance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Like Ms Usha Chandradas and Mr Don Wee, we recognise that the new rules can be complex and MNEs may need time to become familiar with the rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS has been working closely with businesses and tax professionals over the last two years to prepare MNEs for the changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes consulting businesses on the parameters for DTT and MTT and working with the industry and the Tax Academy to conduct training for tax professionals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS will learn from experience, continue to engage stakeholders and continue to provide guidance on MNEs’ obligations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members, including Mr Mark Lee and Mr Neil Parekh, had expressed concerns about penalties if businesses fail to comply with the new rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Don Wee also asked if IRAS would be adequately resourced to administer the DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS has set up dedicated teams to develop the necessary tax administration processes and IT systems to ensure smooth implementation of the DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, moving on to comments on the potential revenue impact of the DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the short term, the implementation of the DTT and MTT will likely lead to additional revenues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If so, then, as we have indicated, we will invest the revenue wisely to enhance our competitiveness, an approach that is supported by Ms Hazel Poa, Mr Don Wee, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Louis Chua and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, what is still not clear is how much additional revenue we will collect and how long it will last.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And this was the point that was raised by Mr Sharael Taha.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is because MNEs and other governments are also working out their responses to the GloBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Whether we will have sustained revenue gains from BEPS and what our net position will be after taking into account our economic spending plans remains to be seen and is still uncertain.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Chua have suggested that we use the revenue gains to support our healthcare expenditure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree that it is important to support our healthcare expenditure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But waiting to see what comes from DTT and MTT would be far too late.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With respect to revenues from DTT and MTT, Members can be assured that the Government will see how to deploy revenues for the benefit of Singaporeans, to continue investing in our people, our economy and our infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A few Members, including Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Louis Chua, had suggested that BEPS 2.0 would remove the race to the bottom for corporate tax rates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is indeed the intent of BEPS 2.0.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we must also look at the reality.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Whilst BEPS 2.0 may reduce the room for tax competition among countries, it does not reduce competition for investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Hazel Poa was of the view that MNEs are highly unlikely to pack up and leave Singapore just because Singapore is implementing the DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While we certainly hope that that is the case, we would be wise not to take anything for granted or to be complacent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Again, a point that Mr Sharael Taha made.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The global economic landscape has become even more competitive in recent years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, major economies like the US, Germany and Japan are rolling out generous incentives to attract investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That alone should tell you that investments are important to countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But to be clear, Singapore's competitive advantages have never been on tax factors alone, and this was recognised by Members of the House, including Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Mr Louis Chua and Mr Mark Lee.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, Ms Hazel Poa acknowledged that we have strong advantages compared to other countries in the region, such as a highly educated workforce, a well-developed and globally connected financial system and excellent connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, I want to thank all Members, including the Opposition Members, for recognising the Government's efforts in establishing these advantages, which took a long time to build over many years and many decades, and these outcomes have been the result of consistent efforts on the part of the Government in order to create a vibrant and competitive economy over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested that we channel DTT and MTT revenues towards developing productivity and innovative capacity, rather than foreign direct investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, foreign direct investments and productivity and innovation are not mutually exclusive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In fact, encouraging foreign direct investments is one way we can raise productivity and innovative capacity in our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Foreign direct investments have a strong value proposition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They bring with them new technologies, market access and business models that are internationally competitive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, productivity and innovation have always been mainstays of our economic strategy and take prominence in almost every Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, in short, it is not one or the other, but we must have an array of economic strategies in order to grow our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, we will continue to invest in our workers and local enterprise ecosystem, which form the backbone of our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SMEs and local companies with skilled workers and strong innovation capabilities will enhance Singapore's value proposition as an economic hub and strengthen our position in the global supply chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also need to do more to sustain our other areas of competitive advantages, such as a skilled workforce, a vibrant innovation ecosystem, political stability, a strong legal system, quality infrastructure and connectivity, and also a vibrant arts and culture scene.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Louis Chua said he hoped that the additional tax revenues from DTT and MTT would not be effectively returned to the affected MNEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members should not mistake reinvesting the additional tax revenues from DTT and MTT into our broader economy, with returning DTT and MTT to affected MNEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we have no intention to round trip anything in derogation of the GloBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fundamentally, our economic philosophy has always been to support all companies that can bring value to Singapore, not just MNEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This has been done through both tax and non-tax measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Any company that wins in Singapore is a win for Singapore, regardless of whether it is an MNE or SME.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These winners will strengthen our ecosystem and create better jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This philosophy will not change with the introduction of the DTT and MTT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If a company is prepared to make a substantive investment in Singapore, carry out high-value business activities here and provide good jobs for Singaporeans, we stand ready to support them, regardless of whether the company is an SME or MNE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Whatever support we give, we will ensure that it is compliant with the GloBE rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Hazel Poa also suggested that MNEs benefit more than SMEs from our corporate tax system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We should look at this not only from the tax perspective, but also consider the amount of support that the Government provides to SMEs through grants and other schemes that we have.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have always supported our SMEs in their growth and productivity journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also set up SME Centres to support SMEs in exploring solutions to grow their businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also introduced newer schemes more recently, for instance, the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative and the Enterprise Innovation Scheme at Budget 2023, and the enhancement of Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme at Budget 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many of these schemes are available only to SMEs, and, for many schemes, SMEs also receive higher support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This Bill also contains specific support for SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, the enhancements to the Renovation and Refurbishment scheme will simplify compliance and give SMEs more flexibility to manage their cash flow needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Rest assured we will continue to support our workers and SMEs to thrive in a more uncertain and competitive business environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I encourage all SMEs to take advantage of available Government initiatives to grow, digitalise and internationalise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To conclude, the two Bills introduce major changes to our corporate tax regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will continue to work closely with all stakeholders to ensure a smooth transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will also continue to invest in our economic competitiveness so that Singapore remains one of the best places to do business.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For Mr Sharael Taha, I am wondering if he will first acknowledge that BEPS 2.0 will, at the minimum, lead to an increase in net revenue, as has been estimated by several independent studies, such as the OECD or academics like Gabriel Zucman at Berkeley, or perhaps he has his own estimates that would suggest that there would be a net revenue loss, in which case, I hope that he will be able to share this with the House.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If so, I wonder if he would not also agree with me that we should at least plan for the possibility that such a revenue stream, however uncertain, should at least be appropriately channeled to specific uses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, we would expect our fine professionals at MOF to engage in such a scenario analysis, lest the Ministry ends up inadvertently with higher-than-expected revenues, which would implicitly suggest then that we are overtaxing the people over and above the nation's current expenditure needs and, hence, putting a crimp on private economic activity.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Just to answer the query that Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: So, yes, it may increase the short-term revenue.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: However, because we do not know how MNEs will react to it, there may be a possibility that it is not a sustainable gain.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: The point I was truly making was about how we approach this situation when investments are such a critical thing to the survival of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: The point I was making was not to approach this in a simplistic manner and underplay the effect of it and overestimate the benefits of it, to the extent of banking it in such that the increase in corporate taxes alone because of BEPS 2.0 can by itself cover the revenue that is generated by the increase in GST.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: So, it is about how do we approach this situation and about us being more cautious about it, and not count the chickens before the eggs hatch.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He asked whether I could agree that we should not invest in capital for the sake of capital and also to acknowledge the importance of human capital.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This Government never does anything just for the sake of a single thing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This Government is driven, first and foremost, by the well-being of Singaporeans, the importance of making sure that Singaporeans have personal growth, good development that will enable them to have good jobs, good incomes and, therefore, to have good standards of living and to be healthy and to do well in life.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And so, if you look at all that the Government has done, not just in the past years but in the past decades, at the heart of it has been the development of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When we first started out, we talked about education.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If you look at the amount that we put into education, I mean, it is the second highest amount in our Budget.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, from primary and secondary, which was the initial investments into our human capital, we then went, in the last decade, into SkillsFuture, recognising that as people come out into the workforce, they will need to continue to learn to grow.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, in this year's Budget do not forget we had the ITE Progression Award as well as the various SkillsFuture programmes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think where I can wholeheartedly agree with Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is the importance of investment in human capital, which we will do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we also obviously have to do investments into hard capital because we have just spent about two hours discussing the MRT.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If we want people to have a good quality of life, you must have good quality infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we do need to make sure that we have good capital investments as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Buildings, making sure we have homes, making sure that the city is a city in nature.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we can certainly agree that we want the best for Singaporeans and will invest in our human resource.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: What is the current fiscal impact of our existing tax incentives and how will this change with the passing of the Bill?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In other words, is there guidance by MOF to EnterpriseSG or the EDB on the budget for RIC, as this will be directly linked to some of the targets of EDB, such as your fixed asset investment, job creation and so on.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The other question is, in terms of the potential companies that could qualify for the RIC.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of the guidance to be published, would the criteria on the assessment be also published?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And is there any timeline for this, as it was previously mentioned that it was going to be out by the third quarter?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the RIC, Mr Louis Chua's question was on who would get it and what would be the criterion for getting RIC, is that right?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I had mentioned that in my opening speech.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have kept it broad at the moment, but there is a certain sense to that – the development or expansion of manufacturing facilities, setting up of headquarters and services, pursuit of R&D, innovation activities, commodity trading, decarbonisation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will put it out, but as I mentioned in my speech, we are working and engaging with the stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we will make sure that there is appropriate guidance when the time comes for them to implement it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And every time we are asked, Minister Chan Chun Sing flinches because it always goes back to the Ministry of Education (MOE).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have to educate on mental health, we have to educate on being green.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a technical subject; it can be quite complex.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Just on ordinary tax, it is tough enough, let alone international tax rules.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the key thing is to put it out in as ordinary, plain layman language as we can.
